title: Batch & Cache Fidelity Explorer — sampling-based tradeoff analysis
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Create a reusable evaluation artifact (the 'Fidelity Explorer') that uses sampling and slice-driven analysis to map latency vs. response-fidelity tradeoffs across batching and KV cache configuration changes. The output will be a set of compact tradeoff curves, per-slice risk scores, and recommended safe operating points + rollout guardrails for use by Runtime, Release, and Console teams.
background: We frequently tune microbatch size, prefix KV cache TTL, and batching window heuristics to optimize throughput/cost. Small config changes can produce non-obvious fidelity regressions on slices of traffic (e.g., long-form completions or multi-turn chats) while improving average latency. Existing evals produce aggregated latency/quality numbers but lack sampling-driven slice risk quantification and statistically-sound regression tests tied to rollout decisions.
goals: Produce sampling-based latency vs. fidelity curves for a configurable grid of batching/cache parameters
Surface per-slice risk (probability of fidelity regression) and effect size with confidence intervals
Automate a compact report and dashboard linked to PRs that provides safe operating points and suggested canary rollout settings
Integrate with regression alert rules used by Console so config changes trigger the right investigations before wide rollout
scope: Bench harness that exercises host-side inference paths (batching + KV cache) against representative prompt sets and production-sampled slices. Does not include retraining or model-architecture changes. Will target a shortlist of open models used in Hosted tier and two Dedicated instance types (A100 and 8xH100-like profiles).
success_metrics: Fidelity Explorer report generated for each PR touching batching/cache config (>=90% of relevant PRs)
Per-slice regression detection true-positive rate >= 85% on historical replay of known regressions
Median time-to-decision for runtime config rollbacks reduced from 6 hours to <= 2 hours using the artifact
experiment_plan: 1) Define parameter grid: microbatch sizes [1,2,4,8,16], batching window [1ms,5ms,10ms,20ms], KV cache TTLs [0s,30s,120s,600s], prefix cache heuristics (merge/no-merge). 2) For each grid point run N=250 paired queries sampled from production slices (chat-turns, long-form completion, reranking). 3) Collect latencies (p50,p90,p99), token throughput, and fidelity metrics (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, model-specific embedding cosine similarity, and custom response-fidelity scores derived from eval harness). 4) Apply paired bootstrap and permutation tests to estimate confidence intervals for fidelity deltas vs baseline. 5) Summarize per-slice risk and generate recommendation (safe/conditional/unsafe) with suggested canary sizes and SLO headroom requirements.
dataset_and_prompts: Combine: (a) anonymized 30k production-sampled prompts (sliced by intent and length), (b) curated eval sets for long-form summarization and code generation (5k examples), and (c) synthetic stress prompts for KV cache boundary conditions. All datasets live in drive:/prod-evals/2026/fidelity-explorer/ and are referenced by manifest file. PII scrubbed and KMS keys applied per Private deployment rules.
evaluation_harness: Use the existing offline harness extended with: response-fidelity scoring pipeline (normalization + multiple metrics), a replay driver that preserves real inter-arrival distributions for microbatch timing, and an instrumentation shim that toggles KV cache TTL/behavior during runs. Harness will emit JSONL traces to s3://redwood-eval-outputs/fidelity-explorer/ for downstream analysis.
visualization_and_dashboards: A compact dashboard in Console that shows: tradeoff heatmap (latency on x-axis, fidelity delta on y-axis), slice breakdown panel, confidence ribbon per curve, and recommended operating points. Prototype dashboard at https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/fidelity-explorer/eng-214512. Also add a small embedded report artifact link to PR descriptions.
alerting_and_rollout_guardrails: Define alert rules that trigger when a PR changes default batching/cache settings and the Fidelity Explorer reports: (a) any slice shows fidelity degradation with p<0.01 and effect size > 3% absolute, or (b) p90 latency improvement > 25% but at cost of fidelity degradation > 1% on high-risk slices. For 'conditional' recommendations, require canary traffic >= 5% for 24h with regression-eval pass before widening. Add automatic rollback webhook in Console for 'unsafe' changes.
acceptance_criteria: Fidelity Explorer can consume a PR artifact and produce a report within <= 90 minutes for the standard grid
Dashboard displays tradeoff curves and per-slice CI ribbons matching offline artifacts
Regression alert rules fire deterministically for historical regression replay tests and are documented in the runbook
A sample PR (linked below) demonstrates an end-to-end workflow: PR -> Explorer report -> Canary -> rollback decision
open_questions: Which fidelity metrics should be primary for multi-modal outputs (text vs embeddings vs code)? Proposal: composite score (weighted) but require final PM sign-off
Do we require deterministic tokenization alignment in the harness or accept small tokenization variance? Deterministic preferred but may increase engineering effort
How to parameterize canary sizes for Dedicated customers where traffic shaping is constrained?
notes: 2026-02-20: Kickoff with Runtime and Console — agreed on grid and slice taxonomy (short-text, long-text, multi-turn-chat, rerank).

2026-02-26: Built initial replay driver and added paired bootstrap analysis. Early runs show a class of long-form prompts where increasing microbatch from 4->8 reduced p99 latency by 18% but increased hallucination-like edits in summarization slice.
2026-03-03: UX sync — dashboard mock validated, will embed report into PR template. Security confirmed dataset scrubbing approach.
2026-03-09: Added automated report uploader and PR-level link generation. Running historical regression replay for 6 known incidents to calibrate alert thresholds.
